class.name: Box3DBallJoint
class.brief_description: A spherical joint: a point on one body is pinned to a point on the other, free to rotate.
class.description: A ball-and-socket. The bodies are pinned together at this node's origin and may rotate freely, unless the cone and twist limits narrow that down. Ragdoll shoulders and hips, chains, pendulums. The limits are measured about [b]this node's local Z axis[/b]: [member cone_angle] caps how far Z may tilt away from its rest direction, and the twist limits cap rotation about Z itself.

method.name: get_current_cone_angle
method.description: How far the joint axis is currently tilted from its rest direction, in radians. Compare with [member cone_angle], which is the limit rather than the reading.

method.name: get_current_cone_angles
method.description: The current swing as two angles in radians: how far the joint axis is tilted towards the node's local X axis ([code]x[/code]) and towards its local Y axis ([code]y[/code]). Their length is [method get_current_cone_angle]. This is the reading the elliptical cone limits: the joint is inside it while [code](x / cone_angle_x)² + (y / cone_angle_y)² <= 1[/code].

method.name: get_current_twist_angle
method.description: The current twist about the joint axis, in radians.

method.name: get_motor_torque
method.description: Torque the motor applied on the last step, in newton-metres.

members.member: Extra rotational inertia of the relative rotation itself, in kg·m², that is not due to the mass of either body. It resists angular acceleration of the joint about all three axes, so a light body on the end of a chain is not whipped about, and is stable at any substep count. 0 (the default) is none. Applies live.

Gives the elliptical cone a separate limit in each direction: [member cone_angle_x] towards the node's local +X axis, [member cone_angle_negative_x] towards -X, [member cone_angle_y] towards +Y and [member cone_angle_negative_y] towards -Y. Each quadrant between two of those axes is bounded by the quarter-ellipse through its two limits, so the boundary is smooth (the quarter-ellipses meet with a common tangent) and a range that reaches much further one way than the other, such as a hip that flexes 115 degrees but extends 15, needs no rotated node: the node's Z axis can stay on the rest pose. The joint is inside while [code](x / ax)² + (y / ay)² <= 1[/code], with [code]x, y[/code] from [method get_current_cone_angles] and [code]ax, ay[/code] the limits on the side each one is on. Only used while [member elliptical_cone_enabled] and [member cone_limit_enabled] are on. Off (the default) leaves the elliptical cone symmetric, exactly as it was. Applies live.

Half-angle of the allowed cone, in radians. 0 pins the axis, larger values open it up. Box3D accepts 0 to 90 degrees only: this is a half-angle, so 90 is already a full hemisphere of swing, and a larger value trips an assert in a debug build of Box3D. Ignored while [member elliptical_cone_enabled] is on.

Elliptical cone: the largest tilt of the joint axis towards the node's local X axis, in radians (either way, or towards +X only while [member asymmetric_cone_enabled] is on). 0 to 162 degrees (0.9 π); Box3D clamps there. Used while [member elliptical_cone_enabled] is on. Applies live, so a limit can follow another joint (for example hip flexion following the knee).

Elliptical cone: the largest tilt of the joint axis towards the node's local Y axis, in radians (either way, or towards +Y only while [member asymmetric_cone_enabled] is on). 0 to 162 degrees (0.9 π). Used while [member elliptical_cone_enabled] is on. Applies live.

Asymmetric cone: the largest tilt of the joint axis towards the node's local -X axis, in radians. 0 to 162 degrees (0.9 π). Used while [member asymmetric_cone_enabled] is on, when [member cone_angle_x] is the limit towards +X. Applies live, so one side of a range can follow another joint without moving the node.

Asymmetric cone: the largest tilt of the joint axis towards the node's local -Y axis, in radians. 0 to 162 degrees (0.9 π). Used while [member asymmetric_cone_enabled] is on, when [member cone_angle_y] is the limit towards +Y. Applies live.
Restricts how far the joint axis may swing away from its rest direction.

Makes the cone limit elliptical: the joint axis may tilt up to [member cone_angle_x] towards the node's local X axis and up to [member cone_angle_y] towards its local Y axis, along an ellipse in between ([method get_current_cone_angles] reads the tilt), instead of one circular [member cone_angle]. Each angle may exceed 90 degrees. The ellipse is centred on the node's Z axis: for a range that reaches further one way than the other, turn on [member asymmetric_cone_enabled] (or turn the node so its Z axis points at the middle of the range). Only used while [member cone_limit_enabled] is on. Off (the default) leaves the circular cone exactly as it was.

Dry friction in the joint, in newton-metres: a torque that resists any rotation, so a ragdoll limb settles instead of swinging forever. 0 is frictionless. It is shorthand for a motor with a zero velocity target, so it is [b]only applied while [member motor_enabled] is off[/b]; an explicit motor wins. [b]This and the motor share one motor[/b], which is the whole of the interaction between the four: turning [member motor_enabled] on hands the motor to [member motor_velocity] and [member max_motor_torque], turning it off hands it back to this. Changing any of them applies live, without rebuilding the joint, so friction can be nudged on a loaded ragdoll without popping it. Setting this wakes the bodies it holds; [member motor_enabled] and [member max_motor_torque] do not. A body frozen by friction can therefore fall asleep and then ignore the hand-back to an explicit motor -- wake it yourself, or keep [member Box3DBody.can_sleep] off on anything driven this way.

Torque budget for the motor, in newton-metres. Box3D clamps the motor's impulse to this times the step, so at 0 the motor moves nothing; the scene dock warns when [member motor_enabled] is on and this is 0.

Torque ceiling for the pose spring, in newton-metres; 0 (the default) leaves the spring unclamped. A muscle can only pull so hard: with a cap, a spring stiff enough to hold a pose can still be overpowered by a load or an impact instead of winning at any cost. Box3D's own spherical spring has no clamp, so a positive value re-seats the spring onto a hidden companion motor joint between the same two bodies -- the one solver spring with a torque ceiling (its accumulated impulse is clamped to the cap times the sub-step, the same law as [member Box3DMotorJoint.max_spring_torque]). Behaviour notes: [member spring_hertz], [member spring_damping] and [member target_rotation] keep their meaning in either seat, the cap needs [member spring_enabled] on and [member spring_hertz] above 0 to run (the scene dock warns), the companion shows up in the debug draw as a motor joint at the same anchor, and [method Box3DJoint.get_constraint_torque] on this node stops including the spring's share while the cap owns it.
Drives the relative angular velocity toward [member motor_velocity] within [member max_motor_torque] -- how a ragdoll limb is animated rather than merely constrained.
Target relative angular velocity, in radians per second about each axis of the joint frame.
Damping ratio of the spring, non-dimensional. 1.0 is critical damping (no overshoot); below 1 the joint oscillates. Only used while [member spring_enabled] is on.
Adds a spring pulling the joint back toward its rest orientation.
Stiffness of the spring, in cycles per second. Higher is stiffer. Only used while [member spring_enabled] is on.
Orientation the spring drives toward, as frame B relative to frame A. Only used while [member spring_enabled] is on.
Restricts rotation about the joint axis to [member twist_lower] .. [member twist_upper].
Lowest allowed twist about the joint axis, in radians.
Highest allowed twist about the joint axis, in radians.
